title: An Introduction to Riemannian Geometry (Lecture Notes in Mathematics)
description: Author-hosted lecture notes (159 PDF pages, version 1.438 dated 6 May 2026) for a Master's course on Riemannian geometry: differentiable manifolds, the tangent space and tangent bundle, Riemannian manifolds (metrics, arc length, distance, induced metrics, existence via partitions of unity, isometries, homogeneous spaces, normal bundles), the Levi-Civita connection (connections on vector bundles, torsion, metric compatibility, the Koszul formula, Christoffel symbols, submanifolds and the second fundamental form), geodesics (parallel transport, exponential map, minimising property, totally geodesic submanifolds, symmetric spaces), the Riemann curvature tensor (symmetries, sectional curvature, Gauss equation, constant curvature), curvature and local geometry (Jacobi fields, conjugate points, a distance comparison theorem), with appendices on Lie algebras, Sp(n), Riemannian submersions, foliations and Hermitian manifolds. Exercises close each chapter.
rightsNotes: The author's homepage links the PDF directly under 'MATM43 Riemannian Geometry' and the cover states 'The latest version of this document can be found at' the author's URL; neither the page nor the PDF states a licence. Unknown licence means reference-only: Corniversity cites statements and pages and links the learner to the PDF; it never imports, embeds or sends the text to a model.

The notes are a living document (version number and date on the cover). Locators record version 1.438; statement numbers and pages may shift in later versions and must be re-verified when the version changes.
The notes' exercises are the author's; Corniversity exercises are original and only cite the notes' exercises as reading.

Several results are stated with proofs deferred to exercises or to the literature (e.g. Proposition 5.10 refers to Petersen; Fact 5.15 to Munkres); Corniversity lessons supply or cite proofs independently.
Lorentzian or pseudo-Riemannian metrics are not treated; MAT-262's contrast unit uses other sources.
